target_customer: Developers and companies running AI agents that need paid tools such as search, scraping and enrichment
problem: Agents cannot buy tools on their own; humans must create accounts, manage API keys and pick providers.
business_model: Usage-based marketplace and router with per call pricing and a prepaid balance
product_category: AI agent tool router and marketplace (Agentmuxer)

founders.name: Dylan Kelly
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a World Schools Debating Championship 2022 finalist and a NeurIPS co-authored paper.

founders.name: Frank Li
prior_employers: OpenAI (Member of Technical Staff, project lead)
education: University of Washington Seattle, Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Launch post describes Two Sigma, NVIDIA and Amazon roles as internships.

competitors.name: Composio
competitors.what: Managed tool integrations for agents, 250+ pre-built

competitors.name: Smithery
competitors.what: Registry and marketplace of MCP servers

competitors.name: Monid
competitors.what: Also pitched as OpenRouter for agent tools, catalog of 200+ tools

technical_complexity.rationale: Routing with benchmarks and fallbacks, billing and a payment balance across thousands of tools is demanding for two people but uses standard MCP and API plumbing.

defensibility.rationale: Benchmark and outcome feedback data could compound, but many routers and registries exist and providers can be integrated by anyone.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Tempo launched a tool router called Mercator in September 2026 per Bankless; Monid pitched the same positioning.

market_need_then: Agent usage was rising and developers wanted one balance and key for tools; evidence is mostly the founders' pitch and the number of similar launches.

branding.name_origin: Agentmuxer appears to combine agent with multiplexer; this is an inference from the product, not stated by a source, so treat as unconfirmed.
branding.domain_note: Product uses agentmuxer.com; company contact uses amorphiclabs.com; copyright held by Varmorphic, Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: 'Let your agent acquire its own tools'

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Crypto Briefing as launching on Base; otherwise limited.

brand_strength.rationale: Two brand names (Amorphic Labs and Agentmuxer) split attention and Amorphic Labs shares its name with other firms; positioning borrows OpenRouter's recognition.

outcome_analysis: Amorphic Labs is a Summer 2026 company with two technical founders, one from OpenAI. Agentmuxer launched around August 25, 2026 behind a waitlist, yet the live site now says the product is retired and archived, which the YC page does not reflect. The cause is not public; a crowded router market is one possible factor but is not sourced.
notes: Agentmuxer site says it is retired and preserved as an archive (fetched Nov 2026) while YC lists the company Active; a search found no news of a shutdown, so exit stays none and this needs recheck. Funding unverified: Dealroom shows a $125K seed with no investors or date; no round recorded. A Dealroom page also says an earlier Amorphic product made personalized demo videos, which I could not confirm elsewhere.
